answers.explanation: That's the defining feature, and its weakness for computer traffic: the reserved capacity sits idle between bursts.
Bursty traffic is the key reason packet switching won for computers. A shared link carries other traffic while one sender is quiet.
A circuit is a fixed path, so losing any switch on it breaks the call. Packets are forwarded hop by hop, so routers can pick a different next hop.
Each packet is forwarded on its own. Packets of one message can take different routes, and can even arrive out of order.
Sharing means queues, and queues mean variable delay and occasional loss. The Internet leaves recovery to the endpoints (TCP, in Chapter 5).
AUTODIN, the Automatic Digital Network, stored and forwarded whole messages, not small packets.
DECnet connected Digital Equipment Corporation's own computers. Like the other early networks, it solved networking inside one world.
Connecting separate networks to each other is internetworking, the problem the Internet was built to solve and the name of this course.
Networking lets machines share. It doesn't make a single computer compute faster.
